Because MSPs run N-central to manage thousands of client environments, a single compromised instance exposes every tenant beneath it, making rapid patching and instance isolation an urgent priority for affected providers.

title: 18-Year-Old Linux SCTP Flaw Could Let Local Users Gain Root and Escape Containers
blurb: An 18-year-old use-after-free bug in Linux's SCTP networking code, tracked as CVE-2026-64564 and named SCTPhantom, can give a local user root and, per Tencent Zhuque Lab's own testing, escape a container to reach the host. The fix already shipped in stable kernels 7.1.6, 6.18.42, 6.12.101 and 6.6.148 on August 3, so enterprises running older kernels with SCTP reachable should patch now.

title: Microsoft 365 AitM Phishing Hijacks Accounts to Collect Payroll and Finance Emails
blurb: Arctic Wolf Labs detailed an active adversary-in-the-middle phishing campaign that hijacks Microsoft 365 accounts to find finance and payroll staff, using voicemail-themed lures, a six-stage redirect chain through Google and Amazon S3 to evade reputation filters, and residential proxies to mask logins. The campaign hit hundreds of organizations across healthcare, education, manufacturing, government, and professional services last month, and overlaps with the Storm-2755 payroll-diversion cluster Microsoft already tracks.

title: Attacker phished way into US defense supplier's Microsoft 365 account
blurb: IEH Corporation, a US defense electronics supplier, disclosed that an attacker phished an employee's credentials and gained access to the company's Microsoft 365 environment. The breach underscores how a single compromised Microsoft 365 account can expose a defense contractor's email and document stores, keeping identity hardening and phishing-resistant MFA at the top of enterprise procurement priorities.

title: AMD wants to make enterprise inference cheaper and faster with chips from Taalas
blurb: AMD agreed to acquire Taalas, a Canadian startup that etches a trained model's weights permanently into custom silicon, and plans to fold the chips into its Instinct GPU roadmap for lower-cost, higher-throughput data-center inference. Because each chip runs only the model baked into it, analysts warn the approach fits mature, high-volume workloads but fuses chip and model into a single shorter-lived asset that complicates capacity planning and lifecycle management.

title: ShinyHunters called cancer diagnostics biz and tricked staffers into giving them access. Now they've dumped 10.9M email addresses
blurb: ShinyHunters social-engineered staff at a cancer diagnostics firm into granting access, then dumped a database containing 10.9M email addresses. The breach underscores that voice-based phishing still bypasses technical controls, pushing IT leaders to weight identity verification and help-desk callback procedures alongside the endpoint and email defenses that vendors typically pitch.

title: Chinese router vendor denies its firmware contains backdoors – but pauses downloads to fix security issues anyway
blurb: A Chinese router vendor denied that its firmware contains backdoors while simultaneously pausing firmware downloads to patch what it characterized as ordinary security issues. The contradiction hands enterprise network teams a supply-chain headache, since the pause disrupts update workflows and revives procurement scrutiny of Chinese-made edge hardware already facing restrictions in US and allied markets.

title: Proxmox ports itself to Arm with help from Nvidia and Supermicro
blurb: Proxmox ported its open-source Virtual Environment platform to Arm, working with Nvidia and Supermicro to run the hypervisor on Arm-based server silicon. The move gives enterprises a KVM-based virtualization option on Arm hardware as they weigh alternatives to VMware after Broadcom's licensing changes, and it extends Proxmox's reach into the Nvidia and Supermicro server stacks now targeting AI and edge deployments.

title: Unveiling good and bad behaviors on the Agentic Internet
blurb: Cloudflare detailed how its Web Integrity & Trust team scores traffic on the "Agentic Internet," moving from static bot-versus-human checks to continuous behavioral analysis that separates ephemeral Risk from reputation-based Trust. The post shares agentic traffic findings since the launch of Precursor and a simulation that grades a visitor's cursor movements as human or bot, giving site owners a way to allow helpful automation while blocking abuse.

title: DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis steps aside amid Google leadership shake-up
blurb: Alphabet named DeepMind co-founder Demis Hassabis chief scientist and promoted CTO Koray Kavukcuoglu to run DeepMind, while veteran Jeff Dean left with three colleagues to start a company. Alphabet shares fell 4% on the reshuffle, which lands as Google keeps losing senior AI talent to Anthropic and OpenAI and raises questions about continuity for enterprises betting on Gemini and Vertex AI.

title: Intrusion at US healthcare software provider puts 3.8M people's data at risk
blurb: An intrusion at a US healthcare software provider exposed the personal and medical data of 3.8M people, according to a breach disclosure reported by The Register. The incident renews scrutiny on third-party software vendors in healthcare, where a single compromised provider can cascade across every hospital and clinic on its platform and trigger HIPAA liability and breach-notification costs for downstream customers.

title: Snowflake attacker pleads guilty to hack of 165 companies’ data
blurb: Connor Riley Moucka pleaded guilty to hacking 165 organizations that used Snowflake's cloud data warehouse, stealing billions of customer records and extorting millions from victims including AT&T, Ticketmaster, and Neiman Marcus. The breaches stemmed from stolen login credentials rather than a Snowflake platform flaw, underscoring that accounts lacking enforced multi-factor authentication remain the weakest link in enterprise SaaS deployments.

title: Microsoft, Apple Release Fresh Security Updates
blurb: Microsoft patched over a dozen vulnerabilities on August 6 across Active Directory, Azure, Entra, SharePoint, and Teams, including three maximum-severity 10/10 flaws in Planetary Computer Pro, Azure SQL Database, and Teams that enable network-based privilege elevation. Apple fixed a single Screen Sharing authentication bypass (CVE-2026-65400) in macOS Tahoe 26.6.1, Sequoia 15.7.9, and Sonoma 14.8.9.

title: Malware Can Abuse Windows Hello for Business Keys for Persistent Entra ID Access
blurb: Researcher Dirk-jan Mollema demonstrated that malware in a signed-in Windows session can silently invoke the victim's Windows Hello for Business key by treating it as a FIDO2 passkey, authenticating to Entra ID without extracting the key, recovering the PIN, or triggering a biometric prompt. The resulting token carries no device-binding claim, letting the attacker register a new device, obtain a 90-day Primary Refresh Token, and reach Microsoft cloud services with no admin rights.

title: Windows 10 LTSC 2021 has five months before security updates cost extra
blurb: Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2021 reaches the end of its five-year mainstream support in January 2027, after which Microsoft will charge for the extended security updates that keep the OS patched. IT teams running LTSC on point-of-sale, kiosk, and industrial fleets now face a hard budgeting decision: pay per-device for continued patches, migrate to the newer LTSC 2024 release, or move to Windows 11.

title: Surprise AI costs threaten enterprise implementations
blurb: Poor visibility into AI spending has pushed one-quarter of enterprises to delay or cancel AI projects, according to a new report from cost-management vendor Mavvrik. The finding points to a governance gap in AI procurement, where consumption-based pricing and fragmented tooling leave IT leaders without the FinOps controls they already apply to cloud spend.

title: Inside the post-merger IT overhaul at Alaska Airlines
blurb: Alaska Airlines completed its post-merger passenger service system cutover in April, migrating millions of bookings from two separate platforms onto a single Sabre PSS following its $1.9B acquisition of Hawaiian Airlines. The 18-month project, led by CIO Charu Jain, kept both airlines' distinct brands on one operating platform, letting a passenger connect across Alaska- and Hawaiian-branded flights without navigating separate systems.

title: Microsoft Web IQ: Ground your AI agents with up-to-date web data
blurb: Microsoft released Web IQ, an agent-focused web search service that repackages the retired Bing Search APIs and the Bing index into a grounding source for LLM applications, joining Work IQ, Fabric IQ, and Foundry IQ in the company's IQ suite. Delivered through MCP servers alongside the existing enterprise-data IQ products, it lets Azure customers ground agents in fresh public web data without standing up a separate search integration.

title: Exploring Privacy Leakage and Data Disclosure Violations in the MacOS Application Ecosystem
blurb: A study of 1,000 macOS apps found that 85% access user-data APIs without disclosing it, and 49.7% exfiltrate data to advertising entities and hosting providers, 12.5% of which do so with no disclosure. The authors introduce NutriScan, a static and dynamic analysis framework, and argue that macOS's fragmented permission mechanisms let undisclosed tracking persist and complicate Apple's app vetting.

title: Despite federal warnings, thousands of U.S. industrial controllers used in water systems remain exposed online
blurb: Forescout's Vedere Labs found over 4,000 Rockwell Automation and Allen-Bradley controllers exposed directly to the internet, including 22 in cities hit by recent attacks on U.S. water systems, with 65% of the devices located in the United States. The exposure persists despite an FBI and EPA advisory tied to intrusions across at least 12 states, where attackers reached MicroLogix PLCs remotely and changed IP addresses and passwords to lock out utility operators.

title: Amazon DynamoDB now supports real-time vector search at any scale
blurb: Amazon DynamoDB now supports native vector search at general availability, letting teams store embeddings alongside operational data and run similarity queries with single-digit millisecond latency at 99%+ recall without a separate vector store. For shops already standardized on DynamoDB, this removes the dedicated vector database, its sync pipeline, and its licensing costs, folding retrieval for RAG and agentic memory into the same serverless, pay-per-request infrastructure.

title: China launches mysterious probe into security of Palo Alto Networks' products
blurb: China's cyberspace regulator opened a security review into Palo Alto Networks' products, echoing the earlier probes it ran against Micron and other US vendors before restricting their use. Enterprises running Palo Alto firewalls in China should expect procurement friction and possible sales limits if the review turns adverse, adding another US network-security vendor to the list caught in Beijing-Washington tech tensions.

title: Cloudflare wants to provide the operating system for the AI-first enterprise
blurb: Cloudflare released Cloudflare OS, an open-source, browser-based workspace that connects AI agents, enterprise data, internal systems, and workflows, built on Workers, Durable Objects, and its Access ZTNA layer so agents start with zero permissions. The launch bundles new identity, token-spend, and insider-risk tooling, and stays model-agnostic and open source, letting enterprises avoid vendor lock-in and pick their own model providers.

title: Atlassian stock skyrockets more than 30% as cloud growth roars back
blurb: Atlassian shares jumped more than 30% after hours after fiscal Q4 revenue rose 28% to $1.766 billion and cloud revenue accelerated to 31% growth, reversing a deceleration that had the company guiding to just 23% cloud growth in February. Enterprises are deepening platform commitments, with record $1M-plus deals, remaining performance obligations up 44% to $4.817 billion, and Rovo, Atlassian's AI assistant, now used by over 80% of the Fortune 500.

title: Cloudflare shares jump 18% on revenue beat and raised full-year outlook
blurb: Cloudflare shares jumped more than 18% after reporting Q2 revenue of $696.1 million, up 36% year-over-year and ahead of the $664.8 million analysts expected, and raising its full-year forecast. Large customers spending over $100,000 annually grew 27% to 4,698 and now drive 73% of revenue, with dollar-based net retention climbing to 120% as enterprises consolidate more security and network spend onto the platform.

title: Critical Vulnerabilities Patched With Chrome 151 Update
blurb: Google shipped Chrome 151, patching 41 critical- and high-severity flaws, most of them memory safety bugs; users should update now.

title: Broadcom updates VMware security for AI-era threats
blurb: Broadcom introduced new security, automation, and performance capabilities for VMware Cloud Foundation, adding on-premises malware sandboxing, air-gapped threat-intelligence support, API protection, and AI assistants across vDefend and the Avi Load Balancer. The new vDefend 1-2-3 workflow cuts intrusion-prevention deployment from months to weeks, keeping all functions on-premises for enterprises with data-sovereignty and regulatory constraints.

title: Why AI is forcing a rethink of data center cooling
blurb: AI workloads are pushing rack power from the traditional 5–10kW to 60kW or more, with high-end GPU deployments exceeding 100kW per rack and individual GPUs drawing 700W–1,200W, past the roughly 20–30kW ceiling where conventional air cooling stops working efficiently. Cooling has shifted from an operational afterthought to a primary constraint on AI infrastructure growth, forcing enterprises to weigh liquid cooling and higher energy overhead against throttled performance and rising thermal risk.

title: AWS targets AI cost concerns with new Marketplace Insights tool
blurb: AWS added AI Insights to AWS Marketplace, explaining AI product pricing in plain language to help CIOs justify spend before committing.

title: Agentic AI workforce is more than doubling year on year, says Salesforce
blurb: Salesforce's second annual Agentic Enterprise Index found customers grew their production agent workforces from an average of five agents in February 2025 to 13 by April 2026, while average deployment time fell 53% to 1.9 days. The data points enterprise buyers toward broader Agentforce rollouts, though analysts have criticized Salesforce's self-defined Agentic Work Unit metric as disconnected from actual business outcomes.

title: Microsoft decides to retire 'MemberOf' operator in Entra ID dynamic groups, creates backlash
blurb: Microsoft is retiring the MemberOf operator in Entra ID dynamic group membership rules, forcing IAM admins who adopted it during public preview to rebuild affected group configurations. The removal has drawn backlash because the operator never reached general availability, leaving early adopters without a documented migration path and stuck reworking access controls that depended on nested group membership.

title: Minisforum N5 Max review: This on-premises AI appliance is built to serve data and AI workloads
blurb: Minisforum released the N5 Max, a five-bay NAS built on AMD's 16-core Ryzen AI Max+ 395 with 64GB of unified memory, positioning it as an on-premises appliance for running local AI models alongside storage workloads. Reviewers praised the performance, thermals, and dual 10GbE plus USB 4 connectivity, but flagged a poor operating system and high price that undercut its case against NAS rivals like UGREEN.

title: VPN provider built a script to block Microsoft's hidden GDID tracking on Windows —  Windscribe's "deGDID" erases existing identifiers and blocks new ones from being created
blurb: Windscribe released deGDID, an open-source PowerShell script that wipes Microsoft's persistent GDID tracker on unmanaged Windows PCs.

title: Dawn of the neoclouds — the rise of a new class of hyperscaler is here. But can they dominate the AI era?
blurb: Neoclouds like CoreWeave and Lambda have carved out a narrow niche selling GPU capacity that AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud cannot supply at the volume the market wants. The bet is that the compute and energy shortage lasts long enough to justify the capital, but Meta's July move to sell excess compute exposed how fragile these single-product business models are when hyperscalers decide to compete on the same input.

title: HPE extends validity of quoted hardware prices, possibly for months
blurb: HPE extended the validity window on its quoted hardware prices, in some cases holding quotes firm for months rather than the usual weeks. The move gives enterprise buyers more room to complete procurement cycles without re-quoting amid volatile component and tariff-driven pricing, reducing the risk that a signed budget no longer matches the invoice by the time hardware ships.

title: Microsoft starts sending out emails to warn about big Entra ID change to authentication
blurb: Microsoft is emailing Entra ID administrators to warn that it will make passkeys the default authentication method, phasing out password-based sign-in to blunt phishing and token-theft attacks. IT teams should audit their conditional-access policies and passkey enrollment now, since the change alters login flows for every Entra-managed user and could disrupt access for accounts that have not registered a passkey.

title: Deepfakes are targeting your executives. Here’s what actually works
blurb: The author argues that executive deepfakes have moved from theoretical AI risk to active enterprise fraud, citing a cloned CFO video call that nearly authorized a seven-figure transfer and was stopped only by a verification question the impersonators couldn't answer. Detection tooling stays immature: forensics tools work post-incident, and liveness checks built for onboarding don't transfer to live calls, so CISOs should invest in out-of-band verification habits rather than trusting synthetic-media detection products.

title: China puts Palo Alto Networks on notice over security concerns
blurb: The Cyberspace Administration of China opened a security review of Palo Alto Networks products, citing national security and cybersecurity regulations without naming specific products or issues. The probe follows earlier reports that China blacklisted Palo Alto alongside Fortinet and VMware security tools, and it threatens the vendor's mainland footprint across Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou as US-China tech restrictions escalate.

title: US cloud 'kill switch' is as dangerous as ransomware, European businesses fear
blurb: A Proton survey of 1,500 firms in the UK, France, and Germany found that 74% are worried about a US government-imposed cloud "kill switch," ranking the risk roughly on par with ransomware. The exposure is concentrated in a handful of US providers, yet only 44% keep a documented and tested continuity plan, so most would scramble to a new provider under pressure with no proven fallback.

title: Zayo enlists Nvidia to help build dedicated ‘AI corridors’ across the US
blurb: Zayo partnered with Nvidia to build dedicated "AI corridors" across the US, adding six net-new long-haul fiber routes plus overbuilds in 10 high-demand markets to connect emerging AI hubs. Alongside power, fiber has become a top constraint on AI data center buildouts, and the DigitalBridge-owned carrier is positioning its 8,000-route-mile expansion to serve neoclouds and operators racing to bring distributed GPU capacity online.

title: CISA Flags TeamCity CVE-2026-63077 RCE Flaw Under Active Exploitation in the Wild
blurb: CISA added CVE-2026-63077 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after the CVSS 9.8 deserialization flaw in on-premise JetBrains TeamCity came under active exploitation, letting an unauthenticated attacker abuse the agent polling protocol to bypass auth and run arbitrary commands as the server process. A successful hit exposes stored credentials and build artifacts across downstream CI/CD pipelines, and FCEB agencies face an August 8 patch deadline under BOD 26-04.

title: AWS, Google, and Vercel Agent Flaws Let Attackers Trigger Tools Without Running the Model
blurb: AWS, Google, and Vercel patched flaws in their agent frameworks that let forged tool-call payloads reach an agent's dispatch path without a legitimate model turn, bypassing system prompts, content filters, and model-level guardrails entirely. The fixes landed in Bedrock AgentCore, Google ADK 2.5.0, and Vercel's @ai-sdk/harness-codex 1.0.29 and harness-opencode 1.0.28, with blast radius bounded by whatever sensitive tools each agent was already wired to.

title: MIT boffins' TONTOU attack slips through Spectre defenses on Intel and AMD CPUs
blurb: MIT researchers disclosed TONTOU, a speculative-execution attack that bypasses the Spectre mitigations Intel and AMD have shipped since 2018, letting an attacker leak memory across security boundaries on current CPUs from both vendors. Platform teams face another round of microcode and kernel patching with the usual performance tax, and cloud operators running multi-tenant hosts carry the largest blast radius until fixes land.

title: Does Kubernetes DRA Replace HAMi?
blurb: DRA's consumable capacity feature, generally available in Kubernetes v1.34 and on by default since v1.35, lets a pod ask the scheduler directly for a slice of a GPU's memory, absorbing the encoding job HAMi built its mutating webhook and scheduler extender to do. The author argues DRA still doesn't replace HAMi, because in-container enforcement at CUDA-call granularity is a job DRA was never designed for. HAMi's response is to split the two: keep enforcement, and rebuild the encoding on top of DRA across three repositories.

title: Cloudflare OS: an open platform for agents, apps, and work
blurb: Cloudflare open sourced Cloudflare OS, a platform that gives every employee an agent and workspace grounded in company-specific context, systems access, and a shared library of skills and procedures. Any organization can now deploy it, connect it to internal tools, and build live apps against internal systems, following the version Cloudflare rolled out to its entire workforce in May.

title: Zapscape (CVE-2026-64561): Guest-to-Host Escape in KVM/x86
blurb: Security researcher Hyunwoo Kim disclosed Zapscape (CVE-2026-64561), a use-after-free in KVM/x86 shadow MMU emulation that lets an untrusted guest escape to the host and execute code with kernel privileges. The bug threatens guest-host isolation on multi-tenant clouds that expose nested virtualization, and with the embargo lifted, a full proof-of-concept exploit chain is now public on oss-security.

title: ChainDrop supply chain compromise: Anatomy of a self-propagating worm
blurb: Microsoft Threat Intelligence documented ChainDrop, an npm supply chain attack that pushed a self-propagating Shai-Hulud worm variant into more than 400 packages across unrelated publishers, including keyv, flat-cache, and cache-manager. The malware runs from a preinstall hook to harvest npm, GitHub, AWS, Kubernetes, and Vault credentials, then republishes packages under stolen publishing tokens, so any build runner that installed an affected release should be treated as compromised and its credentials rotated.

title: Automating cross-repo documentation with GitHub Agentic Workflows
blurb: The Aspire team documented how they use GitHub Agentic Workflows to turn merged product changes into SME-reviewed documentation pull requests across separate repos, without granting agents broad write-everywhere tokens. For Aspire 13.3 and 13.4, 82 feature-docs pull requests merged at a median of 44.8 hours after the product PR, each reviewed by the engineer who shipped the feature, with no added headcount. The writeup focuses on cross-repo automation, the sharp part most same-repo setups never hit.

title: Proxmox ports itself to Arm with help from Nvidia and Supermicro
blurb: Proxmox ported its Virtual Environment platform to 64-bit Arm with engineering help from Nvidia and Supermicro, extending the open-source hypervisor beyond its longtime x86 base. The port targets Arm server silicon like Nvidia's Grace and Supermicro's Ampere-based hardware, giving platform teams a KVM-based alternative to VMware on Arm without a per-socket licensing bill.

title: 18-Year-Old Linux SCTP Flaw Could Let Local Users Gain Root and Escape Containers
blurb: An 18-year-old use-after-free bug in Linux's SCTP networking code, tracked as CVE-2026-64564 and dubbed SCTPhantom, lets a local user with SCTP reachable gain root, and Tencent's Zhuque Lab says it used the flaw to escape a container to the host. Stable kernels 7.1.6, 6.18.42, 6.12.101, and 6.6.148 shipped the fix on August 3, so anyone running an older kernel with SCTP exposed should patch.

title: Unveiling good and bad behaviors on the Agentic Internet
blurb: Cloudflare's Web Integrity & Trust team detailed how it scores web traffic by continuous behavior rather than static bot-versus-human checks, treating Risk as ephemeral and Trust as reputation built over time to handle sessions that shift between human and agent mid-flow. The post shares agentic-traffic findings since the Precursor launch and includes an interactive simulation that classifies your own cursor movements as human or bot.

title: Cloudflare wants to provide the operating system for the AI-first enterprise
blurb: Cloudflare announced Cloudflare OS, an open-source, browser-based workspace that connects AI agents to enterprise data and internal systems, built on Workers, Durable Objects, and its Access ZTNA layer where agents start with zero permissions by default. Alongside it, the company shipped governed "gatekeeper" connectors plus tooling to track AI identities, token spend, and insider risk, giving platform teams a control plane for agent access rather than another vendor-locked model stack.

title: New NatJack Attacks Hijack TCP Sessions and Spoof DNS by Manipulating NAT Tables
blurb: Researcher Malcolm Stagg disclosed NatJack at Black Hat USA 2026, a NAT attack class where a privileged host behind the same NAT hijacks TCP sessions, spoofs DNS, exposes mapped ports, or exhausts connection tables, with CVEs in Windows Hy-V NAT and Linux Netfilter conntrack. There is no single patch, so mitigation means isolating untrusted workloads and encrypting internal traffic.

title: Agentic AI could force a rethink of enterprise AI server design, researchers say
blurb: Microsoft Azure and University of Texas researchers found that agentic AI workloads repeatedly cross the CPU-GPU boundary, stranding both processors and exposing inefficiencies in GPU-centric inference servers built for standalone LLM requests. One CORAL benchmark ballooned into 580 LLM calls interleaved with 552 tool invocations, ping-ponging between processors hundreds of times and leaving some accelerators saturated while others sat idle.

title: Unifying Workers AI and AI Gateway into a single AI control plane
blurb: Cloudflare is merging Workers AI and AI Gateway into a single control plane, so a single AI binding and unified /ai/ REST endpoint now route requests to any model provider, including Cloudflare's own GPU-hosted models. Teams get observability, logging, billing, and security from one path, with a built-in default gateway that applies without any manual setup.

title: Shadow AI in CI/CD: Threat-modeling the path from developer laptop to Kubernetes
blurb: This CNCF post threat-models Shadow AI across a cloud-native delivery path, from a developer laptop to a running Kubernetes pod, and argues the real risk is access, not chatbot usage. The author's key distinction: an assistant suggesting code leaks data, but an agent holding a Git token, cloud credentials, or a ServiceAccount becomes a non-human identity with real blast radius. Each stage maps to a least-privilege control you can implement today with CNCF and open source projects.

title: Runtime instances: persistent compute for production AI agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
blurb: AWS announced runtime instances for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, a managed EC2-backed compute option for production AI agents that need to run for days, access GPUs, or coordinate multiple agents on a shared host. Sessions persist up to 14 days with stop/restart to cut idle cost, and the service reuses existing AgentCore APIs, identity controls, and observability while pairing with EBS and AgentCore Memory for cross-session recall.

title: eMicro: Real-Time Multi-Hop Access Control for Microservices with eBPF
blurb: This paper introduces eMicro, a path-aware access control system that stops multi-hop attacks in microservice meshes, where each individual service-to-service call looks legitimate but the full request path violates security intent. It encodes policies as deterministic finite automata for constant-time lookups and uses eBPF-based in-kernel request tracing to enforce them without code changes. On DeathStarBench and production traces from Uber, Alibaba, and ByteDance, the authors report 1-microsecond policy checks, 50M policies in 100MB, and 90% lower propagation overhead.

title: Datadog shares plummet despite expectation-topping quarterly results
blurb: Datadog stock closed 19% lower despite second-quarter revenue rising 36% year-over-year to $1.12B, beating the $1.08B consensus. The selloff followed a disclosure that Datadog's largest customer, an unnamed AI provider on a newly renewed nine-figure contract, plans to cut user seats and reduce usage this year.

title: Introducing Radar Researcher: An AI tool for exploring Internet data in plain language
blurb: Cloudflare launched Radar Researcher in beta, an AI tool that answers questions about its global Internet traffic data through plain-language queries that return real, interactive charts. Built on Cloudflare's developer platform, it removes the need to find the right Radar page, set filters, or read API docs, opening the free open dataset to journalists and operators tracking outages in a hurry.

title: How to Optimize Your YouTube Channel for AI Visibility
blurb: YouTube mentions showed a 0.737 correlation with AI visibility in Foundation's study of 8,566 B2B SaaS keywords, the strongest factor measured, ahead of Domain Rating and backlinks. YouTube also landed in Google's top 10 for 80.2% of "demo" searches, 22.5% of "best" searches, and 20% of "vs" searches. The tactical takeaway for B2B teams is that a small library of videos built around buyer questions, with clean titles, chapters, and timestamps, keeps surfacing across Google, YouTube, and AI answers without needing millions of views.

title: Consumers Forget Brands Quickly, and AI Often Can’t Help Them Recover Them, Study Finds
blurb: Only 17% of consumers can confidently recall the last three ads they saw after 24 hours, and 31% now turn to an AI chatbot to recover a forgotten brand name, per a new Adobe survey of 1,002 US consumers. Just half of those chatbot users say AI names the right brand even half the time, leaving marketers exposed on both recall and AI-assisted rediscovery.

title: CryptoJS Weak RNG Behind $5.7 Million in Drains Affects Five Crypto Wallet Apps
blurb: Coinspect traced the Ill Bloom wallet drains to CryptoJS.lib.WordArray.random(), a 12-year-old function that supplied weak entropy for recovery-phrase generation across five wallet apps, including RRWallet, Bexo, and NanChat. The flaw shrank 128- and 256-bit search spaces to roughly 2^39 and 2^47, small enough to brute-force on ordinary hardware, and on-chain analysis puts confirmed theft at a $5.7M lower bound. Any phrase from an affected version stays guessable even in a hardware wallet, so users must generate a new seed and move funds.

title: ether.fi Removes Restaking From weETH, Nearing A Full EigenLayer Exit
blurb: ether.fi removed all restaking exposure from weETH, turning its flagship asset into a plain liquid staking token and isolating restaking in weETHs, a separate Symbiotic-based token. The move unwinds the arrangement that made ether.fi the largest business on EigenLayer, with restaked assets already under 1% of its $3.3B staking base and slated to reach zero in Q3 2026.

title: Crypto market maker Wintermute lands SEC approval to trade equities and ETF blocks
blurb: Wintermute's US arm registered with the SEC and FINRA, securing broker-dealer status that lets it trade US stocks and options, self-clear digital asset securities, and act as an ETF authorized participant. The market maker, which handles over $10B in average daily volume across 60-plus venues, plans to start with crypto-linked markets before expanding into tokenized stocks pending further approvals.

title: Robinhood Chain's DEX Volume Fell 72% While Transactions And Deposits Set Records
blurb: Robinhood Chain's DEX volume fell 72.5% from an $878M peak on Jul. 11 to $241M on Aug. 1, even as transactions, TVL, and stablecoin supply hit record highs. The chain's share of global DEX volume dropped from 16.65% to 4.32%, and over 90% of daily incentive payments now go to depositors rather than trading liquidity.

title: JPYC raises $38 million Series B led by major Japanese logistics firm AZ-COM Maruwa
blurb: JPYC raised 6 billion yen ($38M) in a Series B extension led by logistics firm AZ-COM Maruwa, bringing its total funding to $106M across seven rounds since 2021 to expand its yen-pegged stablecoin. AZ-COM plans to settle payments in JPYC across its network of roughly 2,300 partners including Amazon Japan, marking the first large-scale corporate use of a stablecoin for daily business operations in Japan.

title: Coinbase launches 24/5 US stock trading for UK users, advancing ‘Everything Exchange’ strategy
blurb: Coinbase launched 24/5 trading of US stocks for UK users, extending its exchange beyond crypto as part of a broader "Everything Exchange" strategy to merge traditional and onchain finance. UK CEO Keith Grose framed the move as bridging tradfi and crypto rails, positioning Coinbase against brokers like Robinhood and eToro that already offer equities to European retail traders.

title: Senate delays Clarity Act vote until after August recess, Thune confirms
blurb: The Senate delayed its vote on the Clarity Act, the market-structure bill governing crypto regulatory jurisdiction, until after the August recess, with Majority Leader John Thune confirming it will be queued first when the chamber returns. The slip pushes any resolution of the CFTC-versus-SEC oversight question into September, extending regulatory uncertainty for US-based token issuers and exchanges.

title: Black Lake Launches Harbor Verify to Bring Verifiable Credit to Onchain Markets
blurb: Black Lake Digital Markets launched Harbor Verify, a browser-based tool that lets investors, lenders, auditors, and rating agencies cryptographically confirm that every loan in a tokenized RWA pool passed the pool's published eligibility rules without exposing private borrower data. Reviewers reconstruct the pool's Merkle commitments and verify a zero-knowledge proof against an onchain-anchored rulebook hash, starting with a $25M residential mortgage portfolio.

title: The Trust-Free Aggregation Layer of the Unicity Infrastructure
blurb: This paper describes Unicity's Aggregation Layer, a layer 2 service that lets users transact tokens off-chain while preventing double-spending, using an append-only key-value store periodically certified to a Consensus Layer blockchain. State is digested with Radix Sparse Merkle Trees and proven append-only through an AIR circuit on the Plonky3 STARK toolkit, with no trusted setup. The implementation hits 10,000 insertions per second and millisecond-range verification on a single consumer CPU.

title: Bitcoin tops $65,000 after ‘massive surprise’ US jobs miss
blurb: Bitcoin topped $65,000 after US payrolls fell 23,000 in July against an 80,000 forecast, one of the widest misses on record. The soft print led traders to price out a September Fed rate hike, and risk assets rallied on expectations that policy will stay looser for longer.

title: Wintermute registers as SEC broker-dealer to trade stocks, options and crypto ETFs
blurb: Wintermute registered a US subsidiary as an SEC and FINRA broker-dealer, letting it trade stocks and options from its own account, self-clear digital asset securities, and act as an Authorized Participant for crypto ETFs. The move pushes the market maker, which handles over $10B in average daily volume across 60-plus venues, directly into US equities and traditional-finance rails.

title: Sui to add post-quantum signature schemes for quantum-safe accounts
blurb: Sui is adding post-quantum signature schemes that let users adopt quantum-safe keys without generating a new recovery phrase or changing their existing wallet addresses. The upgrade keeps current accounts and address formats intact while hardening signatures against future quantum attacks, avoiding the migration friction that has slowed post-quantum adoption on other chains.

title: ‘Applesauce’: Michigan judge denies Coinbase bid to block state enforcement of sports event contracts
blurb: A federal judge in Michigan denied Coinbase's motion to block state regulators from enforcing gambling laws against its sports prediction markets, with Judge Shalina Kumar calling the exchange's arguments "applesauce." The ruling leaves Coinbase exposed to state-level enforcement over its CFTC-regulated event contracts, deepening the jurisdictional fight between federal derivatives oversight and state gaming authorities.

title: Bernstein favors CleanSpark on AI execution as MARA awaits first commercial contract
blurb: Bernstein rated CleanSpark Outperform with a $24 target, citing progress on its AI data-center leases, while keeping MARA at $17 as the miner awaits its first commercial AI contract. The split ratings reflect a widening gap in how quickly bitcoin miners are converting hosting capacity into signed AI compute revenue.

title: Bernstein says Circle’s Q2 counters bearish concerns over competition, reserve income
blurb: Bernstein reiterated its Outperform rating and $140 price target on Circle after Q2 2026 revenue hit $701 million, up 7% year over year, with adjusted EBITDA of $143 million and EPS of $0.19 both beating consensus. The firm argued the results counter bearish concerns over stablecoin competition and reserve income, pointing to Circle's trust bank approval, the Sept. 16 Arc mainnet launch, and $180 million in expected Arc presale revenue.

title: More than $30 million stolen in violent crypto attacks in 2026 as France emerges as ‘wrench attack’ hotspot: Chainalysis
blurb: Chainalysis reported that violent "wrench attacks" have stolen more than $30 million in crypto from holders through mid-2026, already pacing to surpass 2025's full-year record of $58 million. France has become the epicenter after a breach of French tax-agency records widened the pool of targetable holders, with 30 publicly known cases logged this year and attacks spreading to Strasbourg, Marseille, and smaller communes.

title: EU watchdogs warn scammers are posing as crypto firms and regulators after MiCA deadline: FT
blurb: European regulators warned that scammers are impersonating licensed crypto firms and financial authorities following the July 1 MiCA authorization deadline, exploiting confusion as unlicensed providers wind down or restrict EU services. The scams lean on the credibility gap created by the transition, targeting users unsure which firms remain compliant and which have lost the right to operate under the new framework.

title: Crypto bill ethics provision could let Trump defer millions in taxes: Bloomberg
blurb: Ethics language under review in pending US crypto legislation could let President Trump defer millions in taxes on his personal crypto holdings, according to Bloomberg. The provision would let holders postpone capital gains until assets are sold, a benefit that applies broadly but stands to reward Trump's stakes in World Liberty Financial and other token ventures.

title: Uniswap's New Launchpad Out-Launched Pons On Its First Day On Robinhood Chain
blurb: Uniswap Labs opened its pools.trade launchpad on Robinhood Chain and passed rival Pons in daily token launches within a day, minting 10,506 tokens on August 5 against Pons's 7,210. The launchpad charges no upfront fee and routes each token into a Uniswap v4 pool with a 0.25% autocompounding LP fee, putting Uniswap in direct competition with the Pons application that settles on its own AMM.

title: Bitcoin miners MARA and CleanSpark post double-digital revenue drops as AI infrastructure pivot continues
blurb: MARA Holdings and CleanSpark reported double-digit revenue declines for the quarter, with MARA down 27% to $174.9M and CleanSpark down 30.5% to $138.0M, as both bitcoin miners logged wide net losses driven partly by fair-value markdowns on their BTC holdings. Both continued expanding high-performance computing and AI infrastructure capacity, with CleanSpark now controlling more than 1.8 GW of power, land, and data-center assets.

title: a16z's Miles Jennings Says Banks Fighting the CLARITY Act Are 'Accelerating Their Own Obsolescence'
blurb: a16z crypto policy head Miles Jennings argued that banks lobbying against the CLARITY Act are accelerating their own obsolescence, since blocking the market-structure bill leaves the GENIUS Act in force and lets crypto intermediaries keep paying yield on stablecoin deposits, the exact outcome banks oppose. Six banking trade groups, including the American Bankers Association, want the bill to tighten its prohibition on interest-like stablecoin rewards, warning it will siphon deposits away from local lending.

title: U.S. unexpectedly shed 23,000 jobs in July, putting Fed rate hikes in question
blurb: The U.S. lost 23,000 jobs in July against forecasts of an 80,000 gain, and prior months were revised sharply lower, pushing odds of a September Fed rate hike below 50% to 46% on CME FedWatch. Stocks, bonds, and gold rallied on the print while crypto barely moved, with bitcoin holding modestly higher at $65,000.

title: Late Ondo founder’s mother seeks control of company and removal of De Bode as CEO
blurb: Kathleen Allman, mother of late Ondo Finance founder Nathan Allman, filed a verified complaint in Delaware's Court of Chancery seeking control of the company and the removal of CEO Ian De Bode, alleging he improperly assumed the role without board approval after her son's death. De Bode called the claims meritless, saying Ondo retains the backing of lead investors and the Ondo Foundation.

title: Coldcard fallout shows up onchain as 210,000 bitcoin leaves old wallets
blurb: Roughly 210,000 BTC moved out of long-term holder wallets over the past week, per Glassnode, the largest such decline since December 2024 and a migration in custody rather than profit-taking. The shift follows the Coldcard breach, which exploited weak firmware randomness to reconstruct recovery phrases and drain as much as $114M, prompting affected users to move funds to freshly generated wallets or regulated custodians near market lows.

title: Coinbase’s Base app will become ‘less Base-centric’ under Cobie, Jesse Pollak says
blurb: Coinbase's Base app will shift to a chain-agnostic trading platform under new leader Jordan "Cobie" Fish, letting users trade assets across multiple crypto ecosystems rather than only Base-native products, creator Jesse Pollak said. Fish, who joined Coinbase via its roughly $375M acquisition of fundraising platform Echo, is adding prediction markets and perpetual futures as the Base chain holds nearly $5B in DeFi assets and clears over $1B in daily trading volume.

title: Ethereum staking token weETH splits from restaking as rewards debate heats up
blurb: Ether.fi removed restaking from its main token weETH, converting it into a plain Ethereum staking token and moving restaking exposure to a new token, weETHs. The split lets holders of the roughly $3.55B staking business choose standard staking rewards or higher-yield weETHs, and arrives as Ethereum researchers propose cutting staking rewards to zero once participation crosses a threshold.

title: XRP leads majors losses as Clarity Act vote slips to September
blurb: Bitcoin held near $64,300, flat on the week, after the Senate left Washington without taking up the Crypto Clarity Act, pushing the market structure vote to at least September. XRP led major losses at 5.5% over seven days, while BNB and Hyperliquid's HYPE outperformed as roughly $626M in spot bitcoin ETF inflows defended support near $63,000 to $64,000.

title: Senate won't vote on crypto Clarity Act before its summer break
blurb: The US Senate will not vote on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act before its August recess, pushing any decision on the crypto market structure bill to September at the earliest. Majority Leader John Thune committed to a vote after the Senate returns on September 14, but unresolved objections from both parties leave the timeline for passing comprehensive token-classification rules this year uncertain.

title: Power struggle erupts at Ondo Finance after founder’s death
blurb: Ondo Finance founder Nathan Allman's estate sued former President and current CEO Ian De Bode in Delaware Chancery Court, alleging he improperly seized control of the tokenized real-world asset issuer after Allman's death in May. The filings ask the court to determine who lawfully controls the firm and to bar major corporate actions until the governance dispute is resolved.

title: Russia cracks down on unlicensed crypto exchanges it claims are linked to Ukraine
blurb: Russia's FSB detained more than 20 people in Moscow City accused of running unregistered crypto exchange offices that moved funds stolen from Russian scam victims, including pensioners, to Ukraine. The agency said it shut down nine cross-border crypto channels but named no exchanges, tokens, or amounts and provided no evidence for the alleged Ukrainian coordination.

title: Why Bitcoin's BIP-110 refuses to die despite near-zero miner support
blurb: BIP-110, a user-activated soft fork proposing a temporary cap on non-payment data in Bitcoin blocks, is heading toward its Aug. 9 mandatory signaling period despite miner support sitting under 3%, far below the usual 55% threshold. Because it activates through nodes rejecting non-compliant blocks rather than a miner vote, the proposal proceeds regardless. The episode is a live test of whether Bitcoin governance runs on economic coordination among node operators rather than miner consensus.

title: Bitcoin whales load up on $1.2 billion in BTC as ETFs attract $750 million
blurb: Bitcoin whales holding 10 to 10,000 BTC have accumulated over 20,000 BTC ($1.2B) since July 29 in a tight range below $65,000, while US spot ETFs pulled in $754.69M this week, their strongest week since April. Price has yet to break higher, and analysts say a decisive close above $65,000 is needed to confirm a sustained recovery.

title: ChainClaw: A Layered Agent Framework for Reliable On-Chain Execution
blurb: ChainClaw is a blockchain-native agent framework that adapts general-purpose LLM agents to on-chain execution, where actions are stateful, adversarial, and economically irreversible. It layers event-driven orchestration, a simulation-based safety pipeline with transaction guards, and an on-chain monitoring runtime, all sharing a cross-layer memory subsystem. The authors report higher safety and task-completion rates than baseline agents across a seven-task benchmark.

title: JPYC raises $38 million Series B led by major Japanese logistics firm AZ-COM Maruwa
blurb: JPYC raised 6 billion yen ($38M) in a Series B extension led by logistics firm AZ-COM Maruwa Holdings, bringing its total raised to $106M to expand its yen-pegged stablecoin. AZ-COM plans to settle payments in JPYC across its network of roughly 2,300 partners, including work tied to Amazon Japan, marking the first large-scale corporate use of a stablecoin for daily business operations in Japan.

title: Crypto market maker Wintermute lands SEC approval to trade equities and ETF blocks
blurb: Wintermute's US arm registered with the SEC and FINRA to gain broker-dealer status, letting the crypto market maker trade US stocks and options, self-clear digital-asset securities, and act as an authorized participant creating and redeeming ETF blocks. The approval gives one of crypto's largest market makers a regulated path onto the NYSE and Nasdaq, joining Ripple, GSR, and Crypto.com in building out US securities operations as crypto and traditional trading converge.

title: Hedge fund cyberattacks tied to BlackFile-linked UNC6671 extortion group
blurb: Google's Threat Intelligence Group linked a recent wave of vishing-driven attacks on Point72, Millennium, Two Sigma, and Citadel to UNC6671, the extortion crew formerly branded BlackFile. GTIG tracked over $10.6M in Bitcoin ransom payments between January and May 2026, with initial demands near $3M settling around $750K, as the group pivoted in July toward hedge funds, private-equity firms, and financial-rating agencies.

title: Cloudflare announces Wallets for AI agent payments
blurb: Cloudflare announced Cloudflare Wallets, a programmable wallet system that lets AI agents pay for APIs, content, and services without human signup or billing flows, with planned support for stablecoins and x402 micropayments over HTTP. Account owners fund wallets and delegate spending to agent-run Virtual Wallets governed by allowances, allowlists, transaction caps, and total spending limits, forming the buyer side of Cloudflare's agentic commerce push alongside its Monetization Gateway.

title: Visa buys BioCatch for $2.4 billion
blurb: Visa acquired BioCatch for $2.4B in cash, extending its value-added services push beyond cards into behavioral biometrics that scores how users type, swipe, and hold their phones across 19 billion banking sessions a month. The deal deepens Visa's network-of-networks strategy after its Tink and Featurespace buys, and positions it to sell fraud-detection and proof-of-human signals as AI agents begin initiating transactions.

title: Coinbase launches 24/5 US stock trading for UK users, advancing ‘Everything Exchange’ strategy
blurb: Coinbase launched 24/5 trading of tokenized US stocks for UK users, extending its "Everything Exchange" strategy to bridge traditional equities and onchain finance. The move pushes Coinbase deeper into brokerage territory against incumbents like Robinhood, while sidestepping US regulatory hurdles by launching first in the UK, where tokenized-equity rules are more permissive.

title: Wintermute registers as SEC broker-dealer to trade stocks, options and crypto ETFs
blurb: Wintermute registered a New York subsidiary as a broker-dealer with the SEC and FINRA, clearing it to trade stocks and options, self-clear digital-asset securities, and act as an Authorized Participant for crypto ETFs. The move puts the crypto market maker, which handles over $10B in daily volume, directly inside U.S. equities plumbing as tokenization pulls digital-asset and traditional-finance rails closer together.

title: Senate delays Clarity Act vote until after August recess, Thune confirms
blurb: Senate Majority Leader John Thune confirmed the chamber will delay its vote on the Clarity Act, the crypto market-structure bill, until after the August recess, telling The Block it will be queued up first thing when lawmakers return. The slip pushes a defined regulatory framework for digital-asset issuance and exchange oversight into the fall, extending the jurisdictional limbo between the SEC and CFTC that fintechs building on crypto rails have to navigate.

title: Google says hackers are calling financial firm employees to hack and extort victims
blurb: Google security researchers reported that hacking groups tracked under the umbrella UNC6671 are voice-phishing employees at major financial and investment firms, calling personal cellphones while posing as coworkers or IT helpdesk staff to steal credentials, MFA codes, and sensitive data for extortion. Reuters named Apollo, Bain Capital, Blackstone, Bridgewater, CME Group, KKR, Moody's, and TPG among targets, underscoring that low-tech social engineering still breaches firms with heavy security budgets.

title: Bernstein says Circle’s Q2 counters bearish concerns over competition, reserve income
blurb: Bernstein reiterated its Outperform rating and $140 price target on Circle after Q2 revenue rose 7% year over year to $701 million, with adjusted EBITDA of $143 million topping estimates and reserve income still driving roughly 95% of the total. Analysts framed the results as a counter to bearish concerns over stablecoin competition and rate-sensitive reserve income, pointing to Circle's trust bank approval and the Sept. 16 Arc mainnet launch as revenue streams not yet in consensus estimates.

title: EU watchdogs warn scammers are posing as crypto firms and regulators after MiCA deadline: FT
blurb: European regulators including ESMA and national authorities warned that scammers are impersonating crypto firms and regulators to defraud investors, exploiting confusion after the July 1 MiCA authorization deadline. The transition period leaves EU clients exposed as unauthorized firms wind down or restrict services, giving fraudsters cover to pose as legitimate providers during a moment when many users are already migrating accounts.

title: Black Lake Launches Harbor Verify to Bring Verifiable Credit to Onchain Markets
blurb: Black Lake Digital Markets launched Harbor Verify, a browser-based tool that lets investors, lenders, auditors, and rating agencies cryptographically confirm every loan in a tokenized pool meets its published eligibility rules without seeing private borrower data. The tool combines onchain rulebook hashes, Merkle commitments, and zero-knowledge proofs, and is going live first on a $25M residential mortgage portfolio, replacing bilateral reports and restricted data rooms with independently testable proofs.

title: ‘Applesauce’: Michigan judge denies Coinbase bid to block state enforcement of sports event contracts
blurb: A federal judge in Michigan denied Coinbase's request to block the state from enforcing gambling laws against its sports prediction markets, with Judge Shalina Kumar dismissing the exchange's arguments as "applesauce." The ruling weakens Coinbase's claim that CFTC oversight preempts state regulators, and signals that prediction-market operators face continued state-level enforcement risk even while pursuing federal cover.

title: Crypto bill ethics provision could let Trump defer millions in taxes: Bloomberg
blurb: President Trump is reviewing ethics provisions in pending cryptocurrency legislation that Bloomberg reports could let him defer millions of dollars in personal taxes, according to language still being negotiated in the bill. The conflict-of-interest question complicates passage of a market-structure framework that fintech and crypto firms have lobbied for, tying the industry's regulatory clarity to scrutiny over the president's personal financial stake.

title: Neues Unicorn: Berliner Fintech Moss knackt Milliarden-Bewertung
blurb: Moss raised €30M from Portage and Cherry Ventures at a valuation topping $1B, making the Berlin corporate-card and spend-management startup Germany's newest fintech unicorn. Cofounder Ante Spittler called the round opportunistic, noting existing cash would have lasted to 2027, as AI-assisted back-office automation drew investors to a platform now managing €7B annually for mid-market clients.
